story.title: Trump Issues Order for Warnings on 'Inaccurate' History at Smithsonian
story.summary: President Donald Trump has issued an executive order requiring the installation of signage at the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History. The signs will warn visitors about what the administration deems 'inaccurate historical information' within the museum. This move follows ongoing accusations from the Trump administration of anti-American bias in the museum's exhibits.

event_overview.title: About US History
event_overview.subject: US History
event_overview.summary: This event concerns a July 24, 2026 executive order directing federal officials to place temporary interpretive signage and exhibits on National Park Service-managed approaches to the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History in Washington, D.C. The order follows a White House review that criticized the museum’s presentation of U.S. history; it is part of a broader administration effort, begun in 2025, to influence historical interpretation at federal sites and Smithsonian institutions.

facts.label: Date and directive
facts.value: President Donald Trump issued the order on July 24, 2026. It directs the Secretary of the Interior, through the National Park Service and in coordination with the White House Domestic Policy office, to install temporary signage along NPS-maintained public sidewalks and walkways leading to the museum.

facts.label: Stated purpose and content
facts.value: The order says the signs are to convey findings from the White House report “Saving America’s Story,” state that museum exhibits should be renovated consistently with that report, and direct visitors to resources the administration describes as accurate information about U.S. history. facts.label: Location
facts.value: The affected museum is the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History, on the National Mall at Constitution Avenue NW between 12th and 14th Streets in Washington, D.C.

facts.label: Institutional governance
facts.value: The Smithsonian, established by Congress in 1846, is an independent federal trust instrumentality. Its administration is vested in a Board of Regents that includes the Vice President, Chief Justice, six members of Congress, and nine citizen members; it is not an executive-branch agency.

facts.label: Broader policy context
facts.value: The July 2026 order expressly builds on Executive Order 14253 of March 27, 2025, which directed administration officials to pursue the removal of what it called improper ideology from Smithsonian properties and to work with Congress on future Smithsonian appropriations.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers this specific federal action concerning signage and related pressure on the Smithsonian’s presentation of U.S. history, not every Smithsonian exhibition decision, governance matter, or broader dispute over historical interpretation.

related_stories.title: Indian Education Minister Resigns Amid Youth Protests Over Exam Scandal
related_stories.summary: Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned as India's education minister following widespread protests by youth over exam paper leaks. The protests, led by a movement referred to as 'Cockroach,' culminated in celebrations among demonstrators after Pradhan's resignation was announced. The movement's leaders indicated that the government had accepted their demands, leading to the decision to end the protests.

related_stories.title: Democrats Select South Carolina for First Presidential Primary in 2028
related_stories.summary: The Democratic National Committee has recommended that South Carolina hold the first presidential primary for the 2028 election cycle. This decision marks a significant shift in the primary calendar, as South Carolina will replace Iowa as the opening contest. The move aims to prioritize representation among Black and Latino voters, with Nevada also scheduled for an early primary.

related_stories.title: International Criminal Court Votes to Remove Chief Prosecutor Karim Khan
related_stories.summary: The International Criminal Court (ICC) has voted to remove Chief Prosecutor Karim Khan amid allegations of sexual misconduct. The decision comes nearly two years after the allegations first emerged. Khan has denied the accusations, which include claims of engaging in an improper relationship with a junior staff member and attempting to prevent her from pursuing her complaint.

related_stories.title: Maine Democrats Set to Nominate Troy Jackson for Senate Race
related_stories.summary: Maine Democrats are convening to select a Senate nominee to replace Graham Platner, with former state Senate President Troy Jackson expected to secure the nomination. Jackson, who comes from a logging family, is preparing to challenge Republican Senator Susan Collins in the upcoming election, which is being closely watched nationally. Collins has significantly outpaced Jackson in fundraising, raising over $16 million compared to Jackson's $1 million since entering the race.
